title: Dupuy 468
contents: A German princely league would admit new members by majority consent, promise pensions, and later bring in the French king.
status: 2/3 pages transcribed; 1 more in part; 2/2 cipher pages deciphered
fields: Ernestus dux and Joachimus; probably Ernst of Brunswick-Lüneburg and Joachim von Maltzan
Eve of Saint Paul, at five in the morning; no year. Context suggests c.1518–1520;1519 remains plausible.
30 symbols, 20 letter signs, 6 in nomenclature, 3 nulls?, 1 unidentified
Interlinear decipherment accompanies most cipher runs on f28r–v,PDF65– 66/Gallica63–64.

excerpt: Tunc optimum erit ut **christianissimus hoc fedus petat velle inire**; hoc modo etiam si aliquando noluissent **esse in federe cu**[m] **christianissimo**, hoc modo **astricti erunt esse confederatores christianissimi.**
translation: Then it will be best for the Most Christian King to ask to join this alliance. In this way, even if some had not wished to ally themselves with him, they will be bound to become his allies.
